chunks: Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abu al-Maghra' Humayd ibn al-Muthanna al-Ajli, from Dharih ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Muharibi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

We are the successors of the Prophets. Then he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) honored Ali (peace be upon him) with a cloak, then taught him one thousand words, each word opening up to one thousand words.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for the Imams to be the successors of the Prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the Imams as the spiritual and intellectual heirs to the Prophets, emphasizing their possession of esoteric knowledge (*'ilm al-batin*). The narrative of the Prophet teaching Ali one thousand words, each unlocking a thousand more, symbolizes the infinite depth of divine wisdom transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt, a concept central to Shia gnosis (*'irfan*).
